The Oyo State Police Command has arrested nine suspects over an alleged robbery in Ibadan, during which valuables worth N8.62 million were reportedly stolen from a motorist and his friends.
The suspects were arrested following an attack on a Toyota Camry occupied by Oyewole Wisdom and his friends in the Agugu area of Ibadan on 18 November.
The Police Public Relations Officer, Ayanlade Olayinka, disclosed this in a statement on Friday.
According to the police, the incident occurred around 4 p.m. as Mr Wisdom drove his newly acquired, unregistered Toyota Camry around the Bus-Stop Gate area. A group of hoodlums reportedly chased the vehicle to the Adekile area, where they attacked its occupants and dispossessed them of their valuables.
“The stolen items include an iPhone 17 Pro Max, an iPhone Air, an iPhone 16 Plus, an 11-gram gold necklace, a 2.5-gram gold ring, two power banks and a Dell laptop, with a combined estimated value of N8,620,000. In addition to the robbery, the assailants inflicted extensive damage on the victim’s vehicle, valued at N10,000,000,” the statement said.
After receiving a report of the incident, operatives of the Agugu Police Division visited the scene and launched an investigation that led to the arrest of nine suspects.
They were identified as Olaitan Adegbite, Oladayo Mohammed, Moruf Mufutau, Toheeb Taofeek, Segun Olalere, Animashun Ibrahim, Gbolarinwa Tajudeen, Ridwan Omotosho and Ajala Opeyemi.

The police said preliminary investigations indicated that the suspects had confessed to their alleged involvement in the robbery and were providing useful information to investigators.
Items recovered from the suspects included an iPhone 16 Plus, two power banks, a vehicle bumper, a car charger and the vehicle key.
The command said the suspects and recovered exhibits would be transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Iyaganku, Ibadan, for further investigation.
The Commissioner of Police, Abimbola Ayodeji Olugbenga, urged residents to remain vigilant, provide credible information to security agencies and report suspicious activities.
He said the suspects would be charged in court after the investigation concluded.
